To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Upper Units of the Ortegal allochthons were formed from continental crust and the Lower Ophiolitie and Upper Ophiolitic units were formed in a subduction setting, and that the Rheic Ocean closed by the collision of the Laurussian and Gondwanan plates in the Late Paleozoic.

the Sm–Nd isotopes of the Upper Ophiolithic Complex in NW Iberian Variscan suture zone indicate that the splay of the Rheic ocean that was closed by the Variscan collision of Gondwana and Laurussia was a complex assemblage of oceanic crust, mantle and continental crust.

the Upper Units and the Upper Ophiolith of the Ortegal complex have different isotopic signatures and that they are both derived from a mixture of mantle and crust sources, which is similar to other Variscan allochthons of NW Iberia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tectonic evolution of the Iberian Massif and its surroundings, with special emphasis on the Variscan Orogeny and its pre-Variscan evolution.
the origin and tectonic significance of the Upper Ophiolith and the Upper Units of the Ortegal complex, NW Iberia.
the origin and evolution of the crust and mantle beneath the Iberian Peninsula, and the tectonic processes involved in the formation and evolution of the Variscides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ortegal allochthons originated in a complex tectonic setting, which involved the closure of the Iberian–Armorican oceanic domain by the collision between the Armorican continental margin and the Iberian continental margin, and the subsequent subduction of the Iberic oceanic crust.
the Upper Ophiolithic assemblage of the Ortegal complex is the result of an accretionary prism, which is a consequence of the closure of the oceanic domain between Gondwana and Laurussia.
the Upper Ophiolith and Upper Units of Ortegal are derived from a mixture of oceanic and continental crust and mantle sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Upper Units of the Ortegal allochthons have a continental origin.
the Upper Ophiolithic Complex is a remnant of the Rheic oceanic crust, whereas the upper allochthonic complex (Upper Units) is a remnant from the Gondwana continent.
the Upper Units of the Ortegal and A Coruña Complexes are derived from a single continental source.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the suture between Laurussia and the Gondwana margin was a complex zone of ocean crust, ophiolites and continental crust, and that the closure of the ocean between the two continents involved the accretion of several different oceanic crustal assemblages and continental crustal blocks.
the Upper Ophiolytic Unit and the Upper Units in the Orteal Complex are not exotic allochthons, but rather are part of the Variscides.
the Variscan suture zone in NW Iberian is a collage of allochthones derived from a variety different oceanic assemblage.
